title: QUIC server-side resumption PSK acceptance architecture
purpose: Define the internal managed-listener ticket store and server PSK acceptance seam without widening public resumption support.
design_summary: Server-issued tickets remain listener-local and in-memory. The ticket issuer records the opaque ticket identity, ticket nonce, lifetime, age-add value, issue timestamp, and resumption master secret in an internal store when server ticket issuance is enabled. Later accepted connections on the same listener can consult that store when a ClientHello offers a pre_shared_key identity. A matching, live ticket is accepted only after the server recomputes the resumption PSK and verifies the binder over the binder-truncated ClientHello transcript. Accepted PSK attempts add the ServerHello pre_shared_key selection and derive PSK-DHE handshake traffic secrets from the accepted PSK plus the fresh ECDHE share. Unknown, expired, malformed, duplicate, or binder-invalid offers do not select PSK and continue on the existing full-handshake path when the ClientHello remains otherwise valid. The slice deliberately keeps early_data, server-side 0-RTT admission, anti-replay, external ticket persistence, HTTP/3, and public API changes outside the support boundary.
edge_cases_and_constraints: Ticket lookup is scoped to the same managed listener store that issued the ticket.
Binder validation must use the stored resumption master secret and ticket nonce.
ServerHello pre_shared_key selection is emitted only for one validated identity.
Malformed or duplicate PSK offers are rejected by the existing transcript parse path rather than broadened into general PSK negotiation.
0-RTT, early_data, anti-replay, persistent ticket stores, public API changes, and HTTP/3 stay out of scope.
alternatives_considered: Expose a public resumption-ticket cache. Rejected because public resumption support and persistence are not part of this slice.
Accept any syntactically valid PSK identity. Rejected because binder validation must bind the ClientHello to the stored ticket material.
Open early_data when a ticket is accepted. Rejected because anti-replay and server-side 0-RTT admission remain separate work.
risks: Treating a binder-invalid offer as selected would produce unauthenticated resumed handshakes.
Leaking the listener-local store through public options would widen the support promise prematurely.
Reusing the full-handshake key schedule on accepted PSK branches would break interop because peers derive PSK-DHE handshake keys.
